items.title: Rigidity: the relative dualizing complex inverted along the diagonal gives back the structure sheaf and the complex
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme Y and a proper flat finite presentation morphism f : X -> Y with relative dualizing complex omega, the lemma asserts canonical isomorphisms O_X = c(Lpr_1^*omega) = c(Lpr_2^*omega) (the pre-rigid equation) and omega = c(Lpr_1^*omega otimes^L Lpr_2^*omega) (the rigid equation), where c is the right adjoint of the diagonal Delta : X -> X x_Y X (statement lines 3158-3223). Letting a be the right adjoint of Rf_* and b the right adjoint of p in the cartesian square with q and p the two projections, the proof runs a four term chain: omega = c(b(omega)) because id = c o b as id_X = p o Delta; the second term c(Lp^*omega otimes^L b(O_X)) uses Lemma labelled lemma-compare-with-pullback-flat-proper; the third c(Lp^*omega otimes^L Lq^*a(O_Y)) uses Lemma labelled lemma-proper-flat-base-change and O_X = Lf^*O_Y; and the fourth rewrites a(O_Y) as omega (proof lines 3225-3248). The pre-rigid equation is proved in exactly the same way (proof lines 3250-3252). Recognising the pre-rigid and rigid identities as consequences of id = c o b and the base change comparison for the projection is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
